draft_memo.title: Rooftop Solar Installation Trends in Northstar
draft_memo.body:
In 2025, the Northstar region installed 120 megawatts of rooftop solar capacity, an increase from 100 megawatts in 2024, representing a growth of 20 megawatts over the one-year period [P01]. Installations are measured as new capacity added, not the amount of electricity generated [P01]. Residential rooftop solar installations specifically rose from 40 megawatts in 2024 to 55 megawatts in 2025, marking an increase of 15 megawatts [P02]. Meanwhile, commercial rooftop solar installations saw a smaller increase, growing from 60 megawatts in 2024 to 65 megawatts in 2025, which is an increase of 5 megawatts [P02]. The total rooftop solar installations in Northstar for 2025 reached 120 megawatts, combining both residential and commercial sectors [P01]. 

Additionally, the average installed price of home batteries in Northstar decreased, with Solara reducing its price from 8,000 credits in 2024 to 7,600 credits in 2025 [P04]. This price change reflects the cost of installation but does not include maintenance expenses [P04]. The data on rooftop solar installations is limited to the specified years of 2024 and 2025 and does not account for other factors such as the total number of installations or the geographical distribution of these installations within Northstar [P01]. Furthermore, the figures provided do not include any operational costs associated with these installations, which may affect the overall assessment of the market [P01]. Overall, the data presents a snapshot of the growth in rooftop solar capacity and associated costs in Northstar for the years 2024 and 2025, with specific limitations on the scope of the information provided [P01][P02][P04].
footnotes: [P01] In 2025, Northstar installed 120 megawatts of rooftop solar, up from 100 megawatts in 2024.
[P02] Northstar's residential rooftop solar installations increased from 40 to 55 megawatts between 2024 and 2025. Commercial installations increased from 60 to 65 megawatts over the same period.
[P04] Solara reduced the average installed price of its home battery from 8,000 credits in 2024 to 7,600 credits in 2025. These prices exclude maintenance.

reasons: All claims are properly cited with corresponding footnotes.

  close with the stated data limitations, cited.
